doc_title: Introduction to Programming Languages and Compilers

parsed.title: Introduction to Programming Languages and Compilers
parsed.description: An 8-week course for undergraduate students covering the fundamental principles of programming languages, design paradigms, implementation methods, and the internal structure of compilers.

sections.title: Section 1: Foundations of Programming Languages
topics: Topic 1.1: What is a Programming Language?
Topic 1.2: Programming Domains: From Scientific Applications to Web Software
Topic 1.3: Key Characteristics of a Good Language: Clarity, Orthogonality, Abstraction, and Safety
Topic 1.4: Criteria for Language Evaluation: Readability, Writability, Reliability, and Cost

sections.title: Section 2: Language Design Principles and Paradigms
topics: Topic 2.1: Influence of Computer Architecture: The von Neumann Model
Topic 2.2: Influence of Programming Methodologies: A Historical Perspective
Topic 2.3: The Declarative Paradigm: Functional, Logic, and Query-based Languages
Topic 2.4: The Imperative Paradigm: Procedural and Object-Oriented Programming
Topic 2.5: The Art of Compromise: Common Language Design Trade-Offs

sections.title: Section 3: How Programs Run: Language Implementation Methods
topics: Topic 3.1: Introduction to Translators
Topic 3.2: Compilation: Translating a Program All at Once
Topic 3.3: Pure Interpretation: Executing Line-by-Line
Topic 3.4: Hybrid Systems: The Best of Both Worlds
Topic 3.5: Just-In-Time (JIT) Compilation: A Modern Approach

sections.title: Section 4: Inside the Black Box: The Structure of a Compiler
topics: Topic 4.1: Overview of the Compilation Process: Front-end and Back-end
Topic 4.2: Phase 1: Lexical Analysis (Scanning)
Topic 4.3: Phase 2: Syntax Analysis (Parsing) and Parse Trees
Topic 4.4: Phase 3: Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) Generation
Topic 4.5: Phase 4: Semantic Analysis (Static and Type Checking)
Topic 4.6: Phase 5: Intermediate Code Generation
Topic 4.7: Optional Phases: Code Optimization

sections.title: Section 5: The Compiler's Ecosystem and Applications
topics: Topic 5.1: Real-World Applications of Compiler Technology
Topic 5.2: Related Tools: Preprocessors, Assemblers, Linkers, and Loaders
